newsitem.title: USA: FBI identifies seven people sought in bomb probe.
newsitem.headline: FBI identifies seven people sought in bomb probe.

text.p: The FBI said on Friday it identified seven of the nine people wanted for questioning in the Olympic park bombing investigation just hours after releasing their pictures to the public.

Federal investigators immediately began setting up interviews with the seven, some of whom came forward by calling a special bomb hotline, in hopes of closing in on whoever planted a 40 pound pipe-bomb packed with nails at a crowded outdoor concert.
All nine had been seen in the vicinity of a sound and light tower Centennial Olympic Park between 12:15 and 12:45 a.m., when the FBI said the bomb was set in place.
The device, concealed in a military-style backpack and left beneath a green wooden bench at the base of the tower. It exploded at 1:20 a.m., leaving two people dead and injuring more than 100.

Of the people shown in four photographs and one composite drawing released by the FBI at an afternoon news conference on Thursday, investigators said they were still trying to pin down the identities of two lone men.
One blurry figure in an enhanced photograph, described as a man with short dark hair, was pictured standing at the base of the tower with a backpack hanging from his shoulders.

The second man, shown in a composite drawing with a goatee, was seen by several people sitting on the bench sometime after 12:30 a.m. He was described as being in his 20s, standing nearly six feet tall and weighing between 140 and 170 pounds.
The FBI appeared gratified by the success of the initiative, noting that the seven people identified had been tracked down by midnight Thursday.
"It's been very helpful. It identifies who these people are so we can talk to them," said Jack Daulton, the FBI agent who heads the investigation.

One of the seven people identified, a woman from suburban Atlanta, told the local Fox affiliate that she had tried to contact the FBI before the news conference but never received a response from the agency.
